analysis:
Only landing/package-lock.json changed. It is a dependency bump of the landing site: next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 (and @next/* SWC binaries), sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5 with libvips 1.3.4 and new wasm32 variants (freebsd-wasm32, webcontainers-wasm32), next's nested postcss 8.4.31 to 8.5.23, nanoid, source-map-js, undici 7.30.1, @swc/helpers, and baseline-browser-mapping. It also adds bundled dev/optional @emnapi and @napi-rs entries for tailwind oxide-wasm32-wasi. All resolved URLs I saw point to registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity values. I saw no git, tarball or alternate-registry sources, so lockfile integrity looks consistent. sharp drops hasInstallScript, which reduces install-time script execution. Engines moved to >=20.9.0, matching next's existing engine requirement; one entry, sharp-win32-ia32, says ^20.9.0 and is cosmetic and optional.

The landing site is outside the threat model's in-scope components (provider, native runtime, coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, fan helper). It touches no provider code, no TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012 logic, no A-003/A-010/A-015/A-016 assets, and no attestation or authorization paths. No regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption identified. I could not verify the integrity hashes against the registry or review the upstream release contents. The supply-chain risk of the new versions is not provable from the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Hash values were not independently checked.
